label: Removed children placed in compounds and missions
summary: Children removed under the Chief Protector and later the Welfare Branch were held in Kahlin, The Bungalow, Retta Dixon and missions.

label: Care to custody
summary: Every audited child in youth justice had significant contact with child protection; nationally, 94% of those first supervised at 10 had child protection contact.

label: Arrest to bail court
summary: About 40 Aboriginal people a day taken into custody; Aboriginal adults 2.07 times more likely to be refused court bail than similarly placed others.

label: Remand to detention
summary: 82% of detained children unsentenced; average youth remand 56 days; one child held 238 days before charges were dropped.
source_title: ABC: NAAJA youth justice submission (3 Feb 2026)

label: Prison to child removal
summary: A parent imprisoned or remanded leaves no one to care for children, who are removed. Widely reported by communities; no NT figure found yet.

label: Release into homelessness
summary: More than half of ex-prisoners nationally are released into homelessness or precarious housing; public housing waits average five years.

label: Poverty read as neglect
summary: Kin blocked from caring because their name is not on the lease, the house is overcrowded, or every adult lacks an Ochre card.

label: Crowding to heart disease
summary: Only 57% of NT First Nations households live in acceptable housing; the poorest housing matches the highest ARF/RHD rates.

label: Hearing loss to school
summary: Childhood ear disease leads to hearing loss, misread at school as non-compliance; 94% of Aboriginal prisoners tested had hearing loss.

label: Truancy to income management
summary: Since October 2025 parents of persistently absent children are referred to income management; 385 referred in term 3, 2026, 208 accepted.

label: Arrest at school
summary: A 13-year-old with disabilities was arrested at school for allegedly shoplifting snacks.

label: Alcohol to arrest
summary: Cheaper alcohol after the floor price was scrapped, no sobering-up shelter in Darwin, and a $925 public drinking fine route people to watch houses.

label: No interpreter, longer remand
summary: Darwin Local Court adjourns almost daily for lack of an interpreter; one client spent nearly two weeks on remand, his case adjourned three times.

label: Transfer off Country
summary: Alice Springs children flown to Holtze, families sometimes not told, no assured way home after release.

label: Fast-tracking over Country
summary: The Territory Coordinator can override NT laws including the Heritage Act; it cannot override the Land Rights Act.

label: Evacuation and shelter to policing
summary: Evacuees held in crowded centres under heavier policing; YiSSA residents moved 100 km away. No data yet links this to later arrests.

label: Punitive expeditions clear Country
summary: Police and settler reprisals cleared land for pastoral runs; around half of all recorded massacres nationally were by police or government forces.
